info.title: UCP Shopping Service
info.description:
Canonical REST interface for UCP Shopping service. Schema references are logical pointers - actual payload shape is determined by negotiated capabilities.

**Endpoint Resolution:** This spec defines operations only. The base URL MUST be obtained from the merchant's discovery profile at `/.well-known/ucp` under `services["dev.ucp.shopping"][transport=rest].endpoint`. The `{endpoint}` server variable below is a placeholder for tooling compatibility.

servers.description: Merchant-provided endpoint from UCP discovery profile

get.description: Get the latest state of a checkout session.

put.description: Update Checkout is a full replacement operation. A new Update Checkout operation is not permitted while Checkout status is `complete_in_progress`. Duplicate requests remain subject to Replay Protection. If the Business receives a new Update Checkout request in that state, it leaves the Checkout unchanged and returns the current Checkout with a recoverable error Message.

200.description: Current Checkout state after the Update request, whether the update was applied or rejected.

get.description: Get the latest state of a cart session.

post.description: Cancel a cart session. Returns the cart state at time of cancellation.
Search for products in the business's catalog.
Lookup one or more products by ID with explicit market context. Supports batch lookups of multiple items in a single request.

get.description: Get the current state of an order. Returns the full order entity as a current-state snapshot. The business verifies the requesting platform created the checkout that produced this order.

200.description: Order retrieved or business outcome message

post.description: [Requires the `dev.ucp.shopping.order_modification` extension to be negotiated; see the extension specification. Proposed, not approved.] Admit a cancellation attempt against an Order. State-changing: requires a signed Idempotency-Key and Content-Digest. New requests are checked against `base_order_version` before admission; a stale version returns `stale_order_state` and creates no record. A same-key, identical-bytes retry replays the original response without re-execution, even if the Order has advanced since. Admission returns 201 with the durable modification record; `awaiting_business_decision` is admitted-but-not-committed.

201.description: Attempt admitted (any per-operation outcome, including awaiting_business_decision) or original response replayed.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`. Modification and reconciliation responses are sensitive (order state, idempotency-scoped records) and MUST NOT be cached or prefetched by intermediaries.

200.description: Business outcome before admission (stale_order_state, unknown_modification_unit, operation_not_supported_for_unit, modification_not_supported, invalid_modification_request, not_found, unauthorized). No modification record was created.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`. Modification and reconciliation responses are sensitive (order state, idempotency-scoped records) and MUST NOT be cached or prefetched by intermediaries.

403.description: Authenticated but not permitted (for example missing `dev.ucp.shopping.order:manage`).

409.description: `idempotency_conflict`: the Idempotency-Key was reused with different raw body bytes. Nothing was executed.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable, including idempotency storage failure. Fail closed: nothing was executed. Include Retry-After.

get.description: [Requires the `dev.ucp.shopping.order_modification` extension to be negotiated; see the extension specification. Proposed, not approved.] Read the authoritative, current record of an admitted attempt. Not an idempotent mutation: no Idempotency-Key. Scoped to the authenticated Platform and Order; a record outside that scope is reported as not_found.

200.description: Modification record or business outcome (not_found, unauthorized).

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`. Modification and reconciliation responses are sensitive (order state, idempotency-scoped records) and MUST NOT be cached or prefetched by intermediaries.

get.description: [Requires the `dev.ucp.shopping.order_modification` extension to be negotiated; proposed, not approved. A Business MUST reject the call with `modification_not_supported` when it was not negotiated.] STRICTLY READ-ONLY (safe, RFC 9110 section 9.2.1): never installs a tombstone, claims a key, or changes whether the original request can later commit, so retrying or prefetching it is harmless. Recover an attempt whose create response was lost. Scope is the authenticated Platform, the Order, the `operation` query parameter, and the original key in the `Original-Idempotency-Key` header. `status: found` returns the record; `status: unresolved` is provisional and the Platform MUST NOT create a replacement attempt with a new key on that answer alone. An authoritative negative requires the explicit `fence_modification` operation.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`. Modification and reconciliation responses are sensitive (order state, idempotency-scoped records) and MUST NOT be cached or prefetched by intermediaries.

post.description: [Requires the `dev.ucp.shopping.order_modification` extension to be negotiated; proposed, not approved. A Business MUST reject the call with `modification_not_supported` when it was not negotiated.] Explicit, state-changing, idempotent request that resolves an UNCLAIMED original key into an authoritative non-commit. Requires its own fresh signed Idempotency-Key and Content-Digest (distinct from the original key named in the body). The Business performs one atomic compare-and-set on the scoped key (authenticated Platform, Order, operation, original key): if a claim exists it returns `found` and installs nothing; if the record expired it returns `unresolved`; otherwise it installs a PERMANENT tombstone and returns `fenced`, after which the original request can never commit. A Business that cannot make the tombstone permanent rejects with `fence_not_supported`. The read-only lookup never does this.

200.description: Fence outcome (found, fenced, unresolved) or business outcome (fence_not_supported, modification_not_supported, unauthorized). Replays of the same fence request return the original response.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`. Modification and reconciliation responses are sensitive (order state, idempotency-scoped records) and MUST NOT be cached or prefetched by intermediaries.

403.description: Authenticated but not permitted (for example missing `dev.ucp.shopping.order:manage`).

409.description: `idempotency_conflict`: the Idempotency-Key was reused with different raw body bytes. Nothing was executed.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable, including idempotency storage failure. Fail closed: nothing was executed. Include Retry-After.

post.description: Retrieve complete product detail by identifier. Returns a singular product with a relevant set of variants, exact pricing, and real-time availability. Supports interactive option selection via `selected` and `preferences` parameters for variant narrowing and availability signals.
Merchant sends order lifecycle events to the platform's registered webhook URL. The platform provides the webhook URL during partner onboarding.

checkout_session_id_path.name: id
checkout_session_id_path.description: The unique identifier of the checkout session.

cart_id_path.name: id
cart_id_path.description: The unique identifier of the cart.

order_id_path.name: id
order_id_path.description: The unique identifier of the order.

modification_id_path.name: modification_id
modification_id_path.description: Business-assigned durable modification identifier. The literal `lookup` is reserved for the scoped-key lookup route and MUST NOT be issued as a modification_id.

operation_query.name: operation
operation_query.description: Operation type of the original attempt (for example `cancel`). Part of the lookup scope. The query string MUST be covered by the request signature (`@query`).

original_idempotency_key.name: Original-Idempotency-Key
original_idempotency_key.description: The Idempotency-Key used on the original create request. Carried in a header (not the URL) so it is not recorded in access logs. MUST be covered by the request signature. This is a lookup argument, not an idempotency key for the lookup: the Business MUST NOT store a replay record for, or otherwise treat as state-changing, the lookup request.

authorization.name: Authorization
authorization.description: Should contain oauth token representing the following 2 schemes: 1. Platform self authenticating (client_credentials). 2. Platform authenticating on behalf of end user (authorization_code).

x_api_key.name: X-API-Key
x_api_key.description: Authenticates the platform with a reusable api key allocated to the platform by the business.

signature.name: Signature
signature.description: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature. Required when using HTTP Message Signatures for authentication. Format: `sig1=:<base64-signature>:`.

signature_input.name: Signature-Input
signature_input.description: RFC 9421 Signature-Input header. Required when using HTTP Message Signatures for authentication. Format: `sig1=("@method" "@path" ...);created=<timestamp>;keyid="<key-id>"`.

content_digest.name: Content-Digest
content_digest.description: Body digest per RFC 9530. Required for requests/responses with a body. Format: `sha-256=:<base64-digest>:`.

idempotency_key.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotency_key.description: Ensures duplicate operations don't happen during retries.

request_id.name: Request-Id
request_id.description: For tracing the requests across network layers and components.

user_agent.name: User-Agent
user_agent.description: Identifies the user agent string making the call.

ucp_agent.name: UCP-Agent
ucp_agent.description: Identifies the UCP agent making the call. All requests MUST include the UCP-Agent header containing the signer's profile URI using RFC 8941 Dictionary syntax. The URL MUST point to /.well-known/ucp. Format: profile="https://example.com/.well-known/ucp".

content_type.name: Content-Type
content_type.description: Representation Metadata. Tells the receiver what the data in the message body actually is.

accept.name: Accept
accept.description: Content Negotiation. The client tells the server what data formats it is capable of understanding.

accept_language.name: Accept-Language
accept_language.description: Localization. Tells the receiver the user's preferred natural languages, often with "weights" or priorities.

accept_encoding.name: Accept-Encoding
accept_encoding.description: Compression. The client tells the server which content-codings it supports, usually for compression.

webhook_timestamp.name: Webhook-Timestamp
webhook_timestamp.description: Webhook event occurrence unix timestamp (seconds since epoch).

webhook_id.name: Webhook-Id
webhook_id.description: The unique identifier of a webhook event.

signature.description: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature for response. Contains the signature value in the format `sig1=:<base64-signature>:`.

signature_input.description: RFC 9421 Signature-Input header for response. Describes signed components, timestamp, and key ID.

content_digest.description: JCS-canonicalized body digest per RFC 8785. Format: `sha-256=:<base64-digest>:`.

protocol_error.description: Protocol error body: machine-readable `code` and human-readable `content`.
